prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Hollow-fibre ultrafiltration membranes were operated in continuous cell-recycling fermentation with biofilm accumulation causing transmembrane pressure rise from 0.8 to 2.3 bar over 168 hours, managed by back-flush cycles every 12 hours.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-09281","field":"abstract","quote":"Transmembrane pressure increased from 0.8 to 2.3 bar over 168 h of continuous operation due to biofilm formation"}]},{"text":"Downstream integration between broth rheology and membrane filtration performance is identified as a scale-dependent boundary condition frequently neglected during process development, affecting the interaction between fermentation culture properties and separation efficiency.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-09279","field":"abstract","quote":"Downstream integration—specifically the interaction between broth rheology and membrane filtration performance—is discussed as a scale-dependent boundary condition"}]},{"text":"Research group has operational experience with integrated bioreactor and ultrafiltration membrane systems at pilot scales from 2 to 150 litres, including characterisation of mass-transfer and hydrodynamic parameters relevant to bioprocess design.","sources":[{"id":"R0863","field":"bio","quote":"The group operates a suite of stirred-tank bioreactors (2 L to 150 L)"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has demonstrated experience with ultrafiltration membrane fouling and back-flush recovery [SYN-PUB-09281] and recognises the coupling between broth rheology and membrane performance [SYN-PUB-09279], but the publications focus on hollow-fibre modules for cell recycling in continuous fermentation rather than spiral-wound modules for downstream protease concentration and depth-filter optimisation for biomass removal."}
